title: You’ve heard the story before. Strong man. Long hair. Supernatural power. But you missed the moment that should have shaken you.
paragraphs: You’ve heard the story before. Strong man. Long hair. Supernatural power. But you missed the moment that should have shaken you.
Because it wasn’t the strength that defined him.
It was what he did when he had nothing left.

The scene opens in Judges 15. Dry land. Dust in the air. A man surrounded. No sword. No shield. No army. Just enemies closing in—thousands of them. The Philistines didn’t come to negotiate. They came to end him.
And if you’re honest, you’ve been there too.
Outnumbered. Cornered. No clear way out.
You kept smiling in public, but internally—you knew.

God saw it.
You knew.
Samson wasn’t supposed to be here. He was called. Set apart from birth. A Nazirite. Chosen. But somewhere along the way, compromise crept in. Small at first. Then louder. Then normal.
You don’t fall overnight.
You drift.
And now here he is—facing the consequences of a life that kept flirting with disobedience.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God still moved.
“Then the Spirit of the Lord came mightily upon him…” (Judges 15:14)
Read that again.

Not when Samson was perfect.
Not when he was disciplined.
Right there—in the middle of the mess.
Power.
And what did he have in his hand?
Nothing impressive. No weapon forged in steel. No divine lightning from heaven.
Just the jawbone of a donkey.
“And he found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, put out his hand and took it, and killed a thousand men with it.” (Judges 15:15)
A thousand.
With what should have been useless.
That’s the miracle.
Not just the strength—but the instrument.
God used what was available.
And suddenly this isn’t just Samson’s story anymore.
Because you’ve been disqualifying yourself based on what you don’t have.

No resources.
No influence.
No clean past.
But the truth is—you’re not lacking tools.
You’re lacking surrender.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
Samson didn’t pause to question the absurdity of it. He didn’t analyze whether a jawbone was “suitable.” He moved when the Spirit came.
That’s where many of you hesitate.
You wait until everything feels right. Until you feel worthy. Until your life looks clean enough to serve God.
But Scripture doesn’t say God waits for your perfection.
It says:
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)

While you were still inconsistent.
Still hiding.
Still double-minded.
Jesus didn’t wait.
And neither does His calling.
But don’t romanticize Samson too quickly.
Because the same man who experienced supernatural victory would later collapse under the weight of his unchecked desires.
That’s the tension.
God can use you powerfully…
And you can still destroy yourself if you refuse to repent.
“Your iniquities have separated you from your God…” (Isaiah 59:2)
This is where it turns.
Because the jawbone wasn’t just a weapon.
It was a warning.
God can bring victory in a moment.
But He is after your heart for a lifetime.
You’ve been asking God to fix your battles.
He’s asking you to face your sin.
The miracle isn’t that Samson defeated a thousand men.
The miracle is that God’s Spirit still showed up for someone who had been so reckless with his calling.
And that should hit you.
Because if God still moved in Samson’s life…
Then your story isn’t over either.
But it will be—if you keep playing both sides.
You can’t carry the jawbone in one hand and your secret sin in the other forever.
Something will break.
So here it is.
Not a soft invitation.
A decision.
You either keep drifting—waiting for another crisis to force you back to God…
Or you turn now.
Fully.
“Repent, therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out…” (Acts 3:19)
That’s the line most people avoid.
Repentance.
Not guilt. Not regret.
Turning.
Because grace is free—but it’s not cheap.
It cost blood.
The blood of Jesus Christ.
And He didn’t die so you could stay the same.
He died to make you new.
Say it plainly.
“I’ve been drifting.”
Or
“I need to come back.”
Let it be real.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—real teaching, real correction, real growth—
Because there are two versions of your future.
One where you keep explaining your compromise.
And one where God rewrites your story completely.
